Subject: Control / Data axes — topology sketches for private VPC

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. Per our call, I attached the initial sketches that our networking vendor (NetworkIntegrations LLC) put together for how the control and data planes could be coerced into our colo environment. Two quick asks: 1) can Redwood confirm the control-plane endpoints you need exposed (IPs/FQDNs + ports) for the private-package install, and 2) do you have an opinion on where to terminate mutual TLS for inter-plane traffic?

Notes in the attached PDF: we tried to keep the control-plane in a management VLAN and the data-plane in a high-throughput tenant VLAN; edge attach points are the same leaf switches. The vendor suggested running a lightweight NAT for egress policing on the data plane.

Attachments: plane-boundary-sketch-v0.3.pdf (diagram), ops-swimlane-edge-attachment.png (PNG)

Subject: Re: Control / Data axes — topology sketches for private VPC

Sara — thanks, this is helpful. Quick read and initial answers below; copying Jonas and Kim for ops and install constraints.

Summary answers up front:
- Control-plane endpoints: we need outbound access from the control plane to the Redwood onboarding API (three FQDNs: control.redwood.host, auth.redwood.host, registry.redwood.host) on TCP/443. For on-prem installs we also recommend a NATed static egress IP for telemetry and webhook callbacks — if you prefer non-NATed, we can accept peered routes but need stable /32s.
- Inter-plane mTLS: recommend terminating mTLS on the control-plane side (control plane acts as the TLS server) and enforce client certs from the data-plane nodes; this keeps data-plane tooling simple and centralizes auth.

Actionable comments on the sketches:
1) Management VLAN for control plane — good. Add explicit /26 allocation for control plane hosts so kube control plane, service mesh, and admin proxies don't collide.
2) Data-plane tenant VLAN: keep large MTU (9000) for inference traffic; we will advise on kernel & gRPC keepalive settings in a later patch.
3) Edge attachment: we prefer the edge relay in a DMZ-like L3 hop rather than direct leaf port host routes. That gives us the option to inject prefix-based caching at the relay.

Ops preflight items (Jonas/Kim to confirm):
- Firewalls to allow TCP/443 + 10250 (kubelet) from control into data-plane nodes for rollout hooks.
- Allow connectivity to REDWOOD_PEER (we'll provide FQDNs and cert thumbprints) for KV sync and canary signals.
- For egress proofing, we need sampling-level telemetry (1%) to be routable to your observability collector.

I attached a minimal reference we use for customer handoffs — plane-boundary-sketch-v0.3.pdf has a few annotated callouts. Jonas: can you add the small runbook snippet for certificate rotation and port checks? Kim: confirm the port list and whether kubelet port policy is acceptable.

Thanks,
Priyom
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference

Sara / team — adding ops details and a tiny runbook snippet below. Quoting Priyom for context.

Quoted: 
> Priyom: "Ops preflight items... Firewalls to allow TCP/443 + 10250 (kubelet)..."

Runbook snippet (preflight checks) — run before first staging deploy:
- Check 1: From a bastion in the management VLAN, curl -v https://control.redwood.host/health (expect 200 within 3s).
- Check 2: From control-plane host, ssh -> representative data node and run: nc -zv <data-node-ip> 10250 && nc -zv <data-node-ip> 443. Failure -> capture iptables/nft rules and send to NSK team.
- Check 3: Verify cert chain: openssl s_client -connect control.redwood.host:443 -showcerts; ensure client cert thumbprint matches provided digest.
- Check 4: MTU validation for data-plane path: ip link set dev <iface> mtu 9000; run iperf3 short test to confirm jumbo frames survive across your spine/fabric.

Operational recommendations:
- TLS termination: Jonas agrees with Priyom — centralize TLS on control-plane ingress and require mTLS for RPCs between planes. We will ship a small sidecar that verifies certs (no secret material leaves control-plane).
- KV cache sync: use encrypted gRPC over port 7100 and whitelist only control-plane FQDNs.
- Fallback plan: if the edge relay is unavailable, data-plane nodes should have a soft-fail to local prefix cache (TTL 5m) and queue telemetry for later flush.

Attachments referenced in thread plus a short ops checklist PDF (attached inline to this message in mailbox): ops-preflight-checks-acme-v1.txt (attached as text).

-Jonas
Staff SRE — Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — this is good and captures our main concerns. Quick confirm and next steps:

- We will reserve a /26 in mgmt VLAN and carve out two /29s for control-plane HA pairs as suggested.
- NetworkIntegrations team will switch the proposed edge attach to a DMZ hop and produce an updated diagram by Friday (they acknowledged the cache-friendly relay pattern).
- Acme will open a support ticket with our colo provider to request a static egress IP block for telemetry egress; ETA for that is 7/9.
- Action items for Redwood: please share the exact FQDN list and cert thumbprints (we need them for whitelist and HSM provisioning). Also, can someone from ops provide the small sidecar image name you mentioned so we can pull it beforehand?

Acceptance criteria for our internal sign-off: 1) updated diagram with DMZ hop and explicit /32 static egress routes OR documented peering plan, 2) redwood-provided FQDNs/thumbprints and sidecar image, 3) a signed ops preflight checklist executed in staging (no production cut until staging pass).

I'll mark a follow-up for next Monday to confirm the updated diagram and staging window. Thanks again.

Sara
Cloud Platform Lead — Acme Analytics
